content.comment_body: Hello, I need to create a program that switches on 5 lights (let's say L1 to L5). When the switch is activated, the lights should turn on sequentially at 2-second intervals. For example: One switch should activate the lights from L1 to L5, while another switch should do the same but in reverse (from L5 to L1). I've written a program for this (it's a bit messy), but I'm wondering if there's a simpler, more efficient way to achieve the same functionality with fewer functions. Additionally, I need the lights that were switched on to turn off automatically 10 seconds after being activated. This particular function is just one part of a larger program, which can also activate individual lights from L1 to L5. I'm not sure how to implement this part.

Hi [user_name], I'm a bit confused... Just two days ago, you asked for help controlling two lights, and now it's five?! Was [user_name]'s advice in your previous thread helpful? How did things turn out there? It might be useful to provide feedback in your earlier topic for future readers and to encourage those who assisted you to help again.
Yes, I needed help a couple of days ago regarding a different program. Both have separate purposes. And yes, [user_name]'s suggestions and program were very helpful, and I expressed my thanks.
It seems a bit similar to 'student projects', with common questions about various lamp control circuits. Only the 'Knight Rider' sequence is missing...

Hello. Your solution isn't bad; it's quite readable. You might consider these approaches: 1) User Defined Functions (UDFs) 2) Multiple pages and linking between pages Since you have repeated sections, UDFs can help tidy things up. I suggest checking out the System Manual for [product_name], as well as the in-software help for more details. For linking between pages, use the scissors tool on a link (wire) and see what happens. Try these techniques and let us know your thoughts or ideas.
I've just tried implementing a UDF. It's great! Thank you so much, [user_name]! This has helped me a lot!

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are exploring ways to sequentially control multiple lights, with specific time intervals for activation and an automatic delayed shutdown. The discussion centers around simplifying the logic in [product_name], emphasizing modular methods such as User Defined Functions to reduce complexity and improve readability for beginners.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for an easier and more maintainable solution to sequentially control lights with delayed turn-off in [product_name], preferring reusable components and less complicated program structures.
